memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh stop object is a generic channel: skill-orchestrate routes ANY non-null stop {reason,message} to its conclusion moves (session release, queue archive), and emit_and_exit caches a plan only when a real dispatch row exists. A new blocking invocation-level gate can therefore be added as a new stop reason in the script alone, with no prose in SKILL.md or commands/orchestrate.md. The blocking queue-check gate, by contrast, lives in commands/orchestrate.md, not in the cycle-plan script.

Tracked paths ordinary agent-system operation dirties outside specs/ without any task editing them: .claude-extensions.json (deploy state) and .memory/memory-index.json (retrieval counters), both present in 4 of the last 4 sync/deploy commits. In a repository that owns its source store, <source_dir>/index-entries.json line counts also move, but only as a consequence of a real context-document edit. Any clean-tree predicate must exclude specs/, .claude-extensions.json and .memory/ or it refuses routinely.

guard-destructive-git.sh judges the primary working tree, not the tree a command targets: git checkout -- <path> inside a scratch repository is refused whenever the primary repo is dirty. Build git test fixtures without discard forms; git show HEAD:path > path restores a file without tripping the hook. Also: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD prints the literal HEAD when detached, so branch-equality checks should use git symbolic-ref -q --short HEAD.
